title: Campaign: connectomes, cell types, circuits and repeated copies
abstract: Subcampaign of 'what do connectomes reveal about how nervous systems are built?'. Scope: Groups of neurons: cell-type wiring, motifs, and how similar repeated copies are (left-right, serial homologs, columns, individuals). 26 papers. Status: supported for repeated copies, mixed elsewhere. Serial homologs in the fly nerve cord and in Platynereis are much less similar than left-right copies, mostly through partner types present in one segment only; mushroom-body glomerulus-pair structure repeats in all 21 hemisphere pairs; inhibitory outputs go mostly to same-level targets. Lineage and birth time add little after neuropil overlap: a raw 19.6-fold same-clone excess vanishes with control and reverses at 2 um. Fly wide-field visual neurons of one type share their field and partners (76 of 100 groups) and feed back to their own input types; function was not tested.
